daily.brief: 過去約24小時（11月25日晚上7:30至26日晚上7:56）120個帳號發了350則帖。共同看好最集中的是$SPCX，@elonmusk說SpaceX目前以一個數量級領先世界其他地方而且優勢似乎在擴大；共同看淡只有$BKNG因監管審查與10億美元費用。最熱鬧的$NVDA有62則提及，多空帳號12對7。
daily.full:
共識

共同看好以SpaceX相關與記憶體為主。$SPCX有14個帳號同向：@elonmusk回覆說沒有優勢是不可逾越的，但至少目前SpaceX以一個數量級領先世界其他地方，而且領先優勢似乎在擴大（原帖）；@danielnewmanUV說$SPCX投資年輕美國人的未來（原帖）；@ripster47強調Ripster Clouds在$SPCX $MU上的力量，客戶最佳日子之一，展示波動前的實時入場（原帖）。$MU有9個，@Biotech2k1說下半年買入數據中心和芯片股，聚焦AI的鎬和鏟（原帖）；@TradexWhisperer提到OpenRouter的token量一年內上升35倍，三個月內上升3.5倍，代理工作負載現約佔80%（原帖）；@Micro2Macr0轉推指出MICRON在解放日AVWAP處出現錘頭蠟燭（原帖）。$META有2個，@InvestmentGuru_指出在沒有新聞的情況下錄得當天最佳大市值反轉，開盤575.34美元，低點567.75美元，收盤609.89美元上漲3.4%，接近高點611.06美元，從低點回升7.4%，盤後守住611.43美元（原帖）。

共同看淡

$BKNG有2個帳號看淡。@DougKass批評金融電視上的說話頭缺乏投資流程，引用一些52週低點包括Oracle等（原帖）；@JerryCap說$BKNG受到重大監管審查，並在第三季計提10億美元費用，損害及審查可能持續未來12個月以上（原帖）。

分歧

分歧最大的是$NVDA，62則提及中多空帳號12對7。@techfund1覺得Nvidia推出和運送新產品的節奏真的令人驚嘆（原帖）；@The_AI_Investor說Nvidia對CoWoS先進封裝的需求將在2027年繼續上升，預期增長57%至122萬片晶圓，看起來NVDA並沒有市場預期的需求問題（原帖）。$QQQ多空5對1，$IREN5對1，$SPY4對1。@ACInvestorBlog對$NBIS創下新的盤中高點，詢問收盤預測：90美元或更高？（原帖）。

其他值得留意

$IWM有2個帳號看好，@MikeZaccardi說在縮短的星期五交易時段表現不錯，這將是小盤股自2024年以來最好的一週。記憶體與AI相關討論持續，部分帳號關注供應與訂單。

共同看淡

分歧

$NVDA一週651次提及，多空帳號39對40幾乎持平。SPY 20對10，QQQ 19對8，SPCX 21對6偏向多頭。整體討論量擴大，高提及標的的多空分歧持續存在。

其他值得留意

daily.brief: Over roughly the last 24 hours (7:30pm on Nov 25 to 7:56pm on Nov 26), 120 accounts posted 350 times. Shared bullish views concentrated on $SPCX, where @elonmusk said SpaceX is currently ahead of the rest of the world by an order of magnitude and the lead appears to be widening; shared bearish only on $BKNG due to regulatory scrutiny and a $1 billion charge. The busiest name $NVDA had 62 mentions with 12 bullish versus 7 bearish accounts.
daily.full:
Consensus

Shared bullish views centered on SpaceX-related and memory names. $SPCX had 14 accounts aligned: @elonmusk replied that no advantage is insurmountable, but at least for now SpaceX is ahead of the rest of the world by an order of magnitude and the lead appears to be widening (post); @danielnewmanUV said $SPCX invests in the future of young Americans (post); @ripster47 emphasized the power of Ripster Clouds on $SPCX $MU, one of the best days for clients, showing real-time entries before the move (post). $MU had 9; @Biotech2k1 said buying data center and chip stocks in the second half, focusing on AI picks and shovels (post); @TradexWhisperer noted OpenRouter token volume up 35x in a year, 3.5x in three months, with agent workloads now about 80% (post); @Micro2Macr0 shared a hammer candle on MICRON at the Liberation Day AVWAP (post). $META had 2; @InvestmentGuru_ pointed to the best large-cap reversal of the day with no news, open $575.34, low $567.75, close $609.89 up 3.4% near the high of $611.06, up 7.4% from the low, holding $611.43 after hours (post).

Shared Bearish

$BKNG had 2 bearish accounts. @DougKass criticized the talking heads on financial TV for lacking an investment process, citing some 52-week lows including Oracle (post); @JerryCap said $BKNG is under major regulatory scrutiny and took a $1 billion charge in Q3, with damage and scrutiny possibly lasting more than 12 months (post).

Split

The largest split was on $NVDA, with 12 bullish versus 7 bearish accounts among 62 mentions. @techfund1 said Nvidia's pace of launching and shipping new products is truly amazing (post); @The_AI_Investor said Nvidia's demand for CoWoS advanced packaging will continue to rise in 2027, expected to grow 57% to 1.22 million wafers, and it does not look like NVDA has the demand problem the market expected (post). $QQQ was 5 versus 1, $IREN 5 versus 1, $SPY 4 versus 1. @ACInvestorBlog noted $NBIS made a new intraday high and asked for a close prediction: $90 or higher? (post).

Other Notable

$IWM had 2 bullish accounts; @MikeZaccardi said it performed well in the shortened Friday session and this will be the best week for small caps since 2024. Memory and AI-related discussion continued, with some accounts focusing on supply and orders.

weekly.full:
Consensus

$ORCL had 8 bearish accounts. @CheddarFlow said Oracle's credit default swaps are now wider than Bear Stearns in January 2008, with the bond market pricing the AI build like 2007 (post); @carlquintanilla shared that management fundamentally misunderstands why investors are worried about the AI capex frenzy — not execution risk but counterparty and concentration risk (post). $AMBA and $CAPR each had 5.

$NVDA had 651 mentions for the week with 39 bullish versus 40 bearish accounts, nearly even. SPY 20 versus 10, QQQ 19 versus 8, SPCX 21 versus 6 leaning bullish. Discussion volume expanded overall, with splits persisting on high-mention names.

Other Notable

Cybersecurity names maintained more consistent positive discussion, while ORCL credit concerns accumulated over the week.

Today's Briefing

Over roughly the last 24 hours 120 accounts posted 350 times. SpaceX-related discussion showed strong shared bullish views, with @elonmusk noting a current order-of-magnitude lead that appears to be widening; memory names like MU focused on AI picks and shovels, while META rebounded from a low of $567.75 to close at $609.89 with no news.
